decision: Skenes's 67.5 ERA is a denominator artifact; his career ERA barely moved, but only better-than-career starts will bring it back, so recovery is slow.
ev_analysis: Mean of his past starts (career ~1.97 ERA) as next-start expectation; no way to pose how many starts until the career number recovers.
why: The decision is a recovery path (how a cumulative rate settles over future starts), which a group mean cannot express.

decision: About a 60% chance Alonso hits under .250 in 2026, so the Mets were likely right to let him go.
ev_analysis: Forecast 2026 BA = his 2023-25 mean, .245.
why: The point forecast (.245, under .250) lands on the same call, but the issue's 60% vs 10% split is distributional and the analyst states it as certainty.

decision: No mock draft will be perfect; random gets ~1 of 32, the best analysts ~12, which is real skill against an impossible problem.
ev_analysis: Mean exact matches of best analysts 2021-25 (12.0) vs Kiper (~4) as next year's expectation.
why: Group means give the expected ~12 hits, but 'perfect is impossible' and 'beats chance' need combinatorics and a chance baseline the analyst lacks.

decision: A one-free-transfer rule will cut the portal 35-40% and favor HS-first programs over portal-built ones.
ev_analysis: Mean net portal flow HS-first (-6) vs portal-dependent (+7); no past cases under the new rule to average.
why: The forecast is a counterfactual policy effect; no group of past cases lived under the rule, so no group mean predicts it.

decision: Prepare for Soto to miss 10+ games (54%); expected ~12.6 games lost.
ev_analysis: Mean games missed (and share missing 10+) among position players with calf tightness.
why: The issue's numbers are base rates of calf-tightness outcomes, which is exactly a group mean of past cases.

decision: At 7-14 the Mets project to about 80-82 with a 70-89 interval: bad, not final.
ev_analysis: Mean final win% of past teams that started about 7-14 (or the Mets' own .333 pace) as the point forecast.
why: A slow-start group mean also says 'below .500', but the 'not final' decision rests on the prior and the wide interval the analyst has no way to state.

decision: Early-season stats are mostly noise until they pass their stabilization point (BA ~910 AB, K rate ~60 PA); use the league average until then.
ev_analysis: Either the player's own mean or the league mean; no rule for when to switch.
why: The decision is a model of how a rate settles (reliability by sample size), which the codebook explicitly excludes.

decision: About 11% of teams with a start like the Mets' reach the playoffs; do not confuse P(playoffs|bad start) with P(bad start|playoffs).
ev_analysis: Mean of 0/1 playoffs among teams with a <= .400 start: ~.11.
why: P(playoffs | bad start) is literally a group mean of a 0/1 outcome, so the analyst delivers the headline base rate.

decision: The next 17 games should yield about six wins, not a recovery pace.
ev_analysis: Mets' season win% (.323) x 17 = about 5.5 wins.
why: Lands near six, but from the raw record the issue says understates them and with no opponent-by-opponent conditioning.

decision: The EO's transfer limits cut mid-tier portal intake ~44% vs ~17% for blue bloods, widening the gap Cignetti once crossed.
ev_analysis: Mean portal intake by program type under the old rules; no group exists under the new rule.
why: Projecting a policy that has never operated has no past group to average.

decision: The EO partly restores blue-blood dominance (from ~70% back toward ~80% of titles) and its enforcement lever is dangerous.
ev_analysis: Blue-blood title share by era: 85% pre-portal vs 70% portal era; forecast post-EO as the pre-portal mean.
why: Era means give the 'restoring the old guard' direction, but the partial-restoration size rests on assumptions the analyst would replace with a full reversion to 85%.

decision: An owner index (z-scored, three metrics) ranks owners differently from championship counts.
ev_analysis: Mean win% or titles per owner; no ranking method.
why: The decision is a composite ranking, which the analyst has no tool to build.

decision: Pythagorean says the Mets are about 22-24, a touch unlucky, and still on a ~76-win pace well short of the ~87-win wild card line.
ev_analysis: Mets' current win% (20-26) projected over 162 = about 70 wins; compare with mean wild-card cutoff.
why: Reaches 'short of the wild card' from the raw record, missing the luck separation that is the issue's point.

decision: BaseRuns says the Mets score about what their components earn; they are a thin team, not an unlucky one.
ev_analysis: Mets' mean runs per game vs league mean (bottom third) taken at face value.
why: Same 'thin team' verdict, but by taking runs scored as a fact, which is exactly the assumption BaseRuns tests.

decision: Forecast a season honestly: lock games with a clear gap, call the rest coin flips, sum to an expected total.
ev_analysis: Each team's Vegas win total as its point forecast; 'no significant gap' read as 50/50.
why: The analyst's 'no difference means coin flip' mimics the JND rule and the mean totals match, but with no stated threshold and point totals presented as precise.

decision: Dipoto's 54% is about the historical WC3 line (~88 wins), so it should be a floor, not a target; at that level you make it only sometimes.
ev_analysis: Mean AL WC3 cutoff 2022-24 (88.3 wins = 54.5%); share of ~88-win teams making the playoffs.
why: The decision is a group mean of past cutoffs, which the analyst computes directly.

decision: The Sabres tanked perfectly but the best lottery odds (20%) still lose four times in five.
ev_analysis: Share of worst-record teams winning the #1 pick under the lottery (~20%).
why: The decision is a base rate of a 0/1 outcome for worst teams, which a group mean delivers.

decision: The record-worst Bobcats held only a 25% shot at Davis; best odds are still a long-shot.
ev_analysis: Share of worst-record NBA teams winning the #1 pick (~25%).
why: Same as the Sabres piece: the point is a group base rate of a 0/1 outcome.

decision: The Mets' lopsided roster is Soto alone over a weak floor, a shape no quadrant-average shows.
ev_analysis: One-way ANOVA of OPS by team; read team means (Mets below the .722 median).
why: The group mean says 'mediocre lineup' while the issue's finding is about the spread within the team, an average where a spread was needed.

decision: Matching 16-3 champions are surprising (~0.2% a year) but not destiny; record matches happen about once in eight years.
ev_analysis: Share of NBA (2/24) and NHL (1/39) champions at 16-3; share of years with matching records (3/23).
why: Every number in the decision is a proportion within a group of past champions.

decision: Peer enforcement in college football runs out of energy because each act costs the enforcer.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: A game-theory argument about incentives has no groups or outcomes to average.

decision: Caitlin Clark's nearest statistical twin across NBA history is Oscar Robertson.
ev_analysis: none possible

decision: By eight league rates, 2026 most resembles 2021.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Nearest-neighbor matching of seasons cannot be posed with group means.

decision: The 2026 Mets' twin is the 2012 Mariners; strategy decides which future follows.
ev_analysis: none possible

decision: The Astros' five nearest analogs were all closing windows; none stayed a dynasty.
ev_analysis: none possible (analog group formed by distance, not available)
why: The comparison group is defined by a distance metric the analyst does not have.

decision: Calling Notre Dame the 2026 national champion despite the checklist saying only 'contender'.
ev_analysis: Title rate of teams leading returning production / top preseason contenders.
why: The group base rate says 'contender, stay calm', which is the checklist answer the issue explicitly bets against.

decision: Hosts reach the semis 59% of the time, but the edge has faded and no host has won since 1998.
ev_analysis: Share of hosts reaching semis (13/22), split by era.
why: The decision is a group base rate (and era means show the fade).

decision: Add the three-point line and Clark's twin dissolves; she is the first who is both Robertson and Curry.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Profile matching across dimensions is not a group comparison.

decision: With 22 buyers and 8 sellers, deadline winners are the teams that overpaid (winner's curse).
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Auction theory about bidding has no group mean that forecasts it.

decision: Only five teams pass both the talent and maturity gates; they are the real title threats.
ev_analysis: Factorial ANOVA: title rate by blue-chip (high/low) x returning production (high/low); contenders = high-high cell.
why: Cell means can point to the same five, but titles are rare and the analyst would state the cell rate as certain.

decision: The coin-flip collisions (Ohio State-Texas at 1.5) are the most informative games of the season.
ev_analysis: Win rate of small favorites (~50%) as the forecast.
why: The group mean gives a coin flip but cannot pose the information value of a game, which is the decision.

decision: The 138-QB ranking refutes itself: raters disagree and a QB cannot be ranked apart from his offense.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Rater reliability and ranking validity are outside the toolset.

decision: Fantasy matchups are decided by high-variance positions, not your highest scorer.
ev_analysis: Mean weekly points by position (QB ~17 highest).
why: Group means point to the best scorer as most important, the opposite of a decision that rests on spread.

decision: A 71% season favorite is about 52% in one sudden-death moment, so the worst losses are favorites at the summit.
ev_analysis: Favorites' per-game win rate in playoff vs regular-season games.
why: Per-game means look alike in both settings, so the analyst sees no difference and misses that the edge lives in repetition (a sequence).

decision: A 29% underdog over a season is about 48% in one game, which is why the greatest upsets happen at the top.
ev_analysis: Underdogs' per-game win rate in single-elimination vs regular season.
why: Mirror of 136: per-game means miss the aggregation over repeated trials that produces the 29-to-48 jump.

decision: A point spread is a calibrated probability: -7 wins about 70 in 100, and favorites cover only ~48%.
ev_analysis: Win rate of favorites by spread band; cover rate of favorites.
why: Calibration by spread band is a set of group means, which is how empirical spread tables are built.

decision: A prediction-market price is a probability (38 cents = 38%), and the courts must decide whether it is a bet.
ev_analysis: Payoff rate of contracts priced near 38 cents.
why: A price-bin mean confirms the frequency reading, but the issue's warning is that a number that looks like a fact is dangerous, which the analyst would ignore.

decision: Trading an unknown prospect for a present need is usually sane; the famous blunders are survivorship.
ev_analysis: Share of traded 19-year-old prospects who became stars (small).
why: 'Almost every unknown 19-year-old stays unknown' is a group base rate.

decision: Flipping a middling team takes about 4 stars in baseball, 1 in basketball, 1 QB in football.
ev_analysis: Mean win gap contender vs middling (~12) divided by mean All-Star WAR (4-5).
why: The baseball answer is arithmetic on group means; the other sports are structural argument either way.

decision: Only one Mets series (Philadelphia) matters, because the schedule rarely meets the teams ahead.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Leverage comes from conditioning inside a season simulation, which group means cannot pose.

decision: 80.3% from 43 yards describes a crowd of kicks, not Parkey's kick; the reference class is a choice.
ev_analysis: Forecast the kick at 80%; t-test clutch vs other 40-49 yd kicks (p=.052, 'no clutch effect').
why: The analyst stops at the group mean as the kick's probability, the very move the issue says tells Chicago nothing.

decision: Tampa Bay is the division's third-best team by runs but will win anyway, because a six-game deficit takes 131 games to clear.
ev_analysis: Share of teams leading by six in late August that win the division.
why: The base rate says Tampa wins, but the decision rests on the rate-versus-deficit mechanism the analyst cannot show.

decision: The Athletics, not the Mets, are the eliminated team with the most power to move others' playoff odds.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Leverage on other clubs' odds requires conditioning within a season simulation.

decision: Oregon's 5th-to-76th spread across systems says more than its consensus rank.
ev_analysis: Mean rank across the 35 systems (~19).
why: The mean rank is exactly what the issue says to look past; the decision needs the spread.

decision: A 25-point win said more about Minnesota than Mississippi State, and blowouts don't carry into the next week.
ev_analysis: Next-week cover rate of teams that beat the line by 20+ (47.9%), read as no effect.
why: The group mean lands 'no carryover', but via p>.05 as proof, and the who-moved question needs a rating update the analyst lacks.

decision: One of two 79-80 teams will win the AL West; about 70% it is the worst division winner ever.
ev_analysis: Share of division winners below .500 since 1969 (0 of 270).
why: The historical group mean says it never happens, while the live state makes it about 70% likely.

decision: A Powerball ticket is a losing bet with near-zero lifetime odds, and the state's 'education money' is players' losses.
ev_analysis: Mean payout per ticket across the draw history vs the price.
why: The mean return shows the loss the argument needs, but the lifetime odds and the tail come from combinatorics, not an average.

decision: Summed playoff probability gives the Cubs 126 hope-days and the Mets one; seasons differ in the middle, not the end.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Hope-days need a daily playoff probability, which only a simulation of the season supplies.

decision: A 24% underdog winning is what a calibrated forecast promises about one time in four.
ev_analysis: Win rate of teams given about a 24% market chance.
why: Calibration is a group mean of outcomes in a probability bin.

decision: Our gloomiest Mets forecast was the most accurate; talking ourselves up made things worse, and only the interval survived.
ev_analysis: Compare absolute errors of the five point forecasts.
why: The error comparison reproduces 'gloomiest was best', but the takeaway that the interval held is unavailable to a point-only analyst.

decision: Bills and Notre Dame are the best bets, yet each wins only ~15 in 100; believe it, don't know it.
ev_analysis: Historical title rate of the preseason or midseason favorite.
why: The favorite's base rate also shows it usually loses, but the issue's decision is about stated uncertainty, which the analyst would drop.

decision: Navy rarely beats Notre Dame (1 in 21) but academies cover as big dogs 31 of 47.
ev_analysis: Win rate of 28-35-point underdogs (17/710); academy cover rate as big dogs (31/47).
why: Both numbers in the decision are group means of 0/1 outcomes.

decision: A lockout is about 5 in 6 likely, but lost games next spring only about 1 in 3, because of when the fight starts.
ev_analysis: Share of new-system fights with a stoppage (10/12) and with lost games (7/12 = 58%).
why: The stoppage rate matches, but the group mean gives 58% lost games where the duration model, timed to a December 1 start, gives about one in three.

decision: Outliving the owner rarely frees a team: 18 of 28 stayed in the family, so a fan of 60 has worse than even odds of seeing the Jets leave the Johnsons.
ev_analysis: Share of teams staying in the family after the owner's death (18/28 = 64%).
why: The base rate says the team probably stays, but the fan's odds need lifetimes and sale rates over time (time-to-event).

decision: Chicago traded about 7 future starter seasons (two late firsts) for about 2.5 good seasons of Simmons: a trade in time.
ev_analysis: Mean starter seasons of comparable DTs from 29-32 (10 men) vs picks 17-32 (95 players).
why: Both sides of the trade are group means of comparable past players.

decision: A questionable player plays two times in three; start there.
ev_analysis: Share of questionable listings who played (9,634/14,346).
why: The decision is a group mean of a 0/1 outcome, the codebook's own example.

decision: Georgia is the likeliest champion at ~28 in 100 (6-60 allowing for rating error); the rest of the field is close to coin flips.
ev_analysis: none possible (12-team bracket too new for a seed base rate)
why: A title chance from bracket simulation with rating uncertainty cannot be posed with group means.

decision: Goals follow a Poisson curve from one average (shutouts ~5-6 per 100), except where trailing teams bend it.
ev_analysis: Share of team-games with zero goals (5.6 per 100).
why: The tallied shutout rate lands, but the issue's lesson is the curve from one number and where hockey departs from it.

decision: Some numbers predict early (velocity, K rate after ~70 batters); ERA and wins take over a season, so watch the fast-settling ones.
ev_analysis: none possible beyond each stat's mean
why: Which numbers stabilize when is a reliability model of how a rate settles, outside group means.

decision: Selling Skubal at 54-58 cost Detroit under one point of title odds, because the prize was already tiny.
ev_analysis: Title rate of teams about 2.5 games out of a wild card in early August (a few in 100).
why: The base rate bounds the cost near zero and lands the call, but the with-versus-without counterfactual comes from simulation the analyst lacks.

decision: A 365-team double-elimination field would play fewer games and crown the best team more often (55% vs 45%).
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Comparing hypothetical tournament formats needs simulation; no past group played them.

decision: Expansion to 76 makes 12-seeds better, raising the 12-over-5 rate about five points, though it would take centuries to detect.
ev_analysis: Historical 12-over-5 upset rate (about one in three) carried forward.
why: The group mean from the old bracket forecasts no change, the opposite of the issue's finding that the base rate is about to expire.

decision: A 14-game streak is worth most in midseason (26 points in May), less in April, and almost nothing in August.
ev_analysis: none possible
why: Streak value conditional on the date and live standings needs a season simulation.
